description: Freedom sounds like a bank account big enough that nobody can tell you what to do. Then you get a little closer to that day and find yourself tangled up in the same habits, screens, snacks, and late-night scrolling that you can’t seem to put down. Plenty of us are still waiting to feel free.
In Part 2 of *Up Here*, Brian Ross takes us to the foot of Mount Sinai and looks at what it takes to experience the freedom God offers.

scripture.text: If you hold to my teaching … you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free … Everyone who sins is a slave to sin … If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.

ideas: Mountains have been life-changing places for Brian, and El Shaddai, one of the Hebrew names for God, may mean “God of the mountains.”
Exodus is the story of people with unfair, unjust lives whom God moved to free. It’s recorded so we can experience deep, soul-level freedom too.
At Mount Sinai, the whole mountain shook with fire, smoke, and thunder, and the people trembled at a distance.

ideas.text: The God of Sinai steps in dangerously and disruptively in order to transform.
A life of genuine freedom includes seeking transcendent experiences and a higher view of our lives, through silent prayer, worship, or a day alone on a mountain.
A life of genuine freedom includes following whoever or whatever is surprisingly good, wherever it goes.
Wherever goodness is in your life, God is there.

ideas: If you have a new problem, read an old book. A book still in print 600 years later has proven good in every kind of culture.

ideas.text: A life of genuine freedom includes choosing some physical restraint to experience life-giving Spirit.
When our bodies get loud, it’s harder to hear God.
Two definitions of freedom: the modern one (do whatever I want and answer to no one)
and the soul version Jesus describes in
, freedom from the desires that enslave us.

ideas: God has been nearer to you than you are to yourself your whole life, whether you know it or not. Will you choose to experience the freedom your Creator offers?
questions: Have you ever felt small in a good way… on a mountain, under the stars, or somewhere unexpected? Describe the moment.

questions.text: . The people trembled and stayed at a distance. Where do you want God close, and where do you tend to keep some distance?
Brian talked about places where we might meet a God who is bigger than we are, like silent prayer, worship, or a day alone on a trail.
Which one sounds best to you, and how could you fit it in this week?
A life of genuine freedom includes following whoever or whatever is surprisingly good, wherever it goes.
Where is surprising goodness showing up in your life right now, and what would it look like to lean in?
Brian described two definitions of freedom: getting to a place where nobody tells you what to do
, and being free from the desires that enslave your soul
. Which one has been your default?
. Jesus says the truth will set you free. What would it feel like to be free from one habit or desire that has a grip on you?

questions: Brian’s students from all over the world gasp at Yosemite, and sometimes someone from the Central Valley admits it’s their first time. What’s something good that’s been close by for a long time that you’ve never really experienced?

extra: What stands out to you about how the Israelites reacted to God’s presence?

extra.text: Have you ever met someone whose example made you want to become a better person? What stood out to you about them?
Jesus suggests that we can think we’re free while actually being controlled by something. What do you think that looks like in everyday life?

extra: Why do you think it’s sometimes so difficult to stop doing something, even when we know it’s not particularly good for us?
Thinking about everything we’ve discussed, what might experiencing a little more freedom actually look like in your life right now?
